Package com.salesforce.multicloudj.docstore.ali

Class QueryPlanner

java.lang.Object
com.salesforce.multicloudj.docstore.ali.QueryPlanner
public final class QueryPlanner extends Object
Translates a docstore query's filter set into the primitives a Tablestore GetRange request needs: a primary-key range [inclusiveStart, exclusiveEnd), a scan Direction, and a server-side column ColumnValueFilter.

Walks the target's (base table or secondary index) ordered key-column list rather than assuming a fixed partition/sort shape.

Two-layer design.

  • Column filter = correctness. Every predicate is (also) emitted as a column filter, so the rows returned are always exactly the matching set, regardless of how tight the key bounds are. This is the safety net under the fiddly bound arithmetic.
  • Key range bounds = efficiency. A best-effort seek so the server scans as few rows as possible. Bounds NEVER over-exclude a matching row (the hard invariant). Where the primitive cannot represent an operator exactly, the bound is widened (looser, scans a little extra) and the column filter trims the surplus — never made tighter than correct.

Composite-key rule (the standard prefix rule for range scans over a composite key): an equality prefix, then at most one range column, then an unconstrained (INF) tail. Predicates that cannot be folded into that structure (e.g. IN/NOT_IN, or an equality after a gap) still appear in the column filter, so they remain enforced.

Boundary representation. For a non-terminal range column we can realize any of >, >=, <, <= exactly using an INF_MIN/INF_MAX tail fill (there is a trailing slot to nudge). For the terminal (last) PK column there is no trailing slot, so the two operators whose exactness needs one — forward > and <= (and the backward mirrors) — are widened by one boundary group and the column filter removes the extra rows.

  • Method Details

    • plan

      public static QueryPlanner.Plan plan(List<String> pkColumns, List<Filter> filters, boolean orderAscending)
      Builds the GetRange plan for a query resolved to a table/index with the given ordered primary-key columns.
      Parameters:
      pkColumns - the target table/index primary-key column names, in key order (never empty).
      filters - the query filters (ANDed). May be empty (full-range scan).
      orderAscending - scan direction: ascending -> FORWARD, descending -> BACKWARD.
